app.name: Universal I/O
app.tagline: Show it a screen and ask about whatever you can't work out.
app.chooseTitle: Choose the screen you need explained
app.chooseLead: The screen you pick appears on this page. Point at anything you don't understand and ask.
app.signInFirst: Asking a question needs a Google sign-in (the same account as the Mac app). This button signs you in and brings you back.
app.pickerTab: Picking from “Chrome Tab” works best. You never have to switch to that tab — it stays on this page while you watch it and ask.
app.pickerOther: Windows and entire screens work too, but for those you have to go to the screen and come back.
app.pickerPrivacy: Of the screens you share, only the one you ask about is sent. The rest stay inside this tab and are gone when you stop sharing.
app.companionTitle: Watch on a phone or tablet
app.companionLead: Mirror this screen onto the device in your hand and ask from there. You can carry on using the computer as normal. Pick “Entire Screen” and it mirrors whatever you're doing.
app.noCaptureNote: This device can't share a screen — phone and tablet browsers don't support screen sharing. Open this page on a computer and press “Watch on a phone or tablet” to get a QR code and a code to type.
app.goBackTitle: Go back to the screen you're stuck on
app.goBackLead: When you come back to this tab, the screen you were looking at appears here.
app.candidates: To ask about a different screen, pick it here (newest first — the ← → keys work too)
app.retake: Retake the screen as it is now
app.watchOnPhone: Watch on a phone or tablet

ask.pointedHere: (pointed at this place on the screen)

join.title: Watch a shared screen
join.lead: Enter the code shown on the computer.

auth.sameAccount: The same account as the Mac app. Sign in on either and you get the same allowance and the same history. Screen images and answers are not stored.
auth.sameAsMac: Same account as the Mac app
auth.failedCheck: Couldn't check whether you're signed in.
auth.expired: Your sign-in has expired. Please sign in again.

companion.modalTitle: Watch on a phone or tablet
companion.scanOrType: Scan it with the camera, or open this page on the other device and type the code
companion.autoClose: This window closes itself once you're connected. Sharing carries on as long as this tab is open, and the computer stays usable.
companion.waiting: Waiting for the other device to connect
companion.connected: Connected. You can ask from the other device
companion.pinchHint: Pinch to zoom · drag a finger to circle
companion.noFrameYet: No picture has arrived yet. Check the connection.
companion.noSession: No session. Please reload the page.

capture.unsupported: This browser can't share a screen. Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer — phone and tablet browsers don't support screen sharing.
capture.no-video-track: Couldn't get any picture from the share.
capture.capture-failed: Couldn't capture the screen. Check that sharing hasn't been stopped.

gatewayError.TIMEOUT: No answer came back in time. Please try again.
gatewayError.NETWORK_ERROR: Couldn't reach the server. Check your connection.
gatewayError.UNAUTHENTICATED: You need to sign in. Please sign in again.
gatewayError.REAUTH_REQUIRED: You need to sign in. Please sign in again.
gatewayError.RATE_LIMITED: Things are busy right now. Please wait a moment and try again.
gatewayError.PROVIDER_ERROR: The AI model didn't respond. Please wait a moment and retry.

sessionError.expired: Your sign-in has expired. Please sign in again.

peerError.no-direct-path: The two devices couldn't connect directly. Check that they're on the same Wi-Fi (connecting across networks needs a relay server, which isn't set up yet).
peerError.connect-timeout: The connection took too long. Check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi.

hero.title: Where are you stuck?
hero.subtitle: Choose a screen, and it explains whatever you point at.
hero.companion: Watch on a phone or tablet

demo.blank: There's nothing here. Being able to say "nothing" is part of the job.

headline.e: This question is the whole app. Point at anything you don't understand, and an explanation appears — like this.
headline.a: This is a scripted demo. The real thing is behind “Choose a screen”, and it does this to your screen.

choose.e: The real thing starts here. Pick one of your screens and it appears on this page.
choose.a: “Chrome Tab” works best — you can watch and ask without ever leaving this page.

companion.e: Turns a phone or tablet into a second pair of eyes. Scan the QR and your screen appears in your hand.
companion.q: Can I keep using the computer?
companion.a: Yes. Work on the computer, ask from the device in your hand.

logo.e: This is the logo. I//O means Input/Output — a name for standing between people and computers.
logo.a: The wall between input and output. That's where we work.

product.e: A link to the product site. The thinking and the mechanics are explained over there.
product.q: And the page I'm on now?
product.a: The app itself. You can try it before reading anything.

pricing.e: A link to pricing. It sits where you can read it before you buy.
pricing.q: Can I try it for free?
pricing.a: Sign in with Google and you can use it right from this screen.

lang.e: The language switch. The page and the AI's answers change language together.
lang.a: The answers come back in Japanese too. Your choice is remembered for next time.

macos.e: The macOS download. The native app can read your screen's real coordinates.
macos.q: How is it different from the web?
macos.a: On a Mac, answers land directly on top of your actual screen. For deep use, this is the one.

legal.e: Company, privacy, terms, commerce disclosure — placed where you can read them before paying.
legal.a: No. Only the one frame you ask about is sent, and neither images nor answers are kept.
